keys.statement: Consider inherent safety from the first flowsheet: once technology and configuration are fixed, changes are costly, and inherently safer design is held to be the most cost-effective risk reduction.

decisions.obstacle: Safety considered only after the route is chosen.
decisions.mechanism: Most degrees of freedom are spent before a safety review.
decisions.operation: Screen routes for inherent safety during conceptual design.

keys.statement: Rank route, unit or stream alternatives early with an index built from chemical indicators (flammability, explosiveness, toxicity) and process indicators (pressure, temperature), both known from a simple flowsheet.

decisions.obstacle: Comparing alternatives on safety with little data.
decisions.mechanism: Indicators available at the concept stage.
decisions.operation: Hazard-, risk- or cost-based index (22, 33 and 18 tools counted).

keys.statement: When flash point, heat of combustion or flammability limits are missing for a pure organic, simple regressions on atom counts, molar mass and normal boiling point can estimate them; the upper limit is the least reliable.

decisions.obstacle: Missing hazard properties at the concept stage.
decisions.mechanism: Correlations from readily known molecular data.
decisions.operation: Estimate, label as estimated, and replace with data later.
limits: Estimated values are derived quantities; keep them apart from measured ones (AGENTS.md).
